target_year_over_year_context.explanation:
Both disclosures state that as a result of the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act, beginning in 2018, Citi is taxed on income from U.S. operations at a federal rate of 21%.

Both disclosures explain that the impact of the federal tax rate change on Citi's state tax rate depends on how individual states choose to adopt the new federal tax law provisions.

comparisons.peer_summary: Statements regarding the expected effective income tax rate are subject to risk that the actual rate may differ due to changes in tax rates, earnings mix, profitability locations, or interpretations of tax statutes and regulations, including global anti-base erosion guidance.
comparisons.comparison: Both Citi and Goldman Sachs disclose that their future effective tax rates are subject to uncertainty and risk of deviation due to changes in tax laws and the specific ways jurisdictions (states or foreign) interpret or adopt federal tax provisions. Citi specifically highlights the risk associated with individual states choosing whether and when to adopt new provisions of the U.S. Internal Revenue Code. Similarly, Goldman Sachs notes that its effective tax rate is subject to risk due to interpretations of existing tax statutes and regulations, as well as corporate tax legislation, including global anti-base erosion guidance.

sentences.text: The effect on Citi's state tax rate is dependent upon how and when the individual states that have not yet addressed the federal tax law changes choose to adopt the various new provisions of the U.S. Internal Revenue Code.

Statements about our future effective income tax rate are subject to the risk that it may differ from the anticipated rate indicated in such statements, possibly materially, due to, among other things, changes in the tax rates applicable to us, changes in our earnings mix, our profitability and entities in which we generate profits, the assumptions we have made in forecasting our expected tax rate, the interpretation or application of existing tax statutes and regulations, as well as any corporate tax legislation that may be enacted or any guidance that may be issued by the U.S. Internal Revenue Service or in the other jurisdictions in which we operate (including Global Anti-Base Erosion (Pillar II) guidance).
